problem.connectFirst.message: Connect {source} with an API key first.
problem.connectFirst.note: source: Brevo, Mailchimp, MailerLite, listmonk, Keila, Notifuse

problem.fileNoKey: File imports don't need an API key: upload the file instead.
problem.fullAddress: Use the full address, like https://lists.example.com.

problem.onlyAddress.message: Use only the server's address, like https://lists.example.com: no credentials, query or fragment.
problem.onlyAddress.note: a fragment is the #part of an address

problem.privateAddress.message: That address is on a private or internal network. Turn on providers.allow_private_networks to import from a server there.
problem.privateAddress.note: providers.allow_private_networks is a config key, never translated

problem.notField.message: {field} isn't a field of this source.
problem.notField.note: field: a source field's key, like FNAME

problem.fieldGone: That custom field doesn't exist any more.
problem.newFieldKey: New field keys use lowercase letters, digits and _.

problem.twoNewFields.note: key: the new field's key, in quotes

problem.pickField: Pick a field from the list.
problem.oneEmail: Map exactly one field to email.
problem.discard: Only drafts and stopped imports can be discarded. Finished imports stay in the history.
problem.running: This import is running. Stop it first or wait for the summary.
problem.finished: This import is finished. Start a new import to bring in more contacts.
problem.listOnce: Each source list can only be imported once.
problem.pickList: Pick a list to import into.
problem.noList: That list doesn't exist in this workspace.
problem.notStagedWait: The rows aren't read from the source yet. Wait for the field mapping to load, then try again.
problem.notStaged: The rows aren't read from the source yet.
problem.mapEmail: Map a field to email before importing.
problem.chooseList: Choose at least one list to import.
problem.pickTarget: Pick the list each source list goes into.
problem.onlyPaused: Only a paused import can be resumed.
source.listmonkAddress: Enter the address of your listmonk server, for example https://lists.example.com.
source.notifuseAddress: Enter the address of your Notifuse instance, for example https://notifuse.example.com.

source.mailchimpKey.message: Mailchimp keys end with the data center, like xxxxxxxx-us21. Copy the whole key from Account › Extras › API keys.
source.mailchimpKey.note: Account › Extras › API keys is Mailchimp's own menu, as its screens say it

source.mailchimpRejected.message: Mailchimp rejected the API key{said} from the {dc} data center. Keys look like xxxxxxxx-{dc}; the suffix must match the data center the account lives in.
source.mailchimpRejected.note: said: Mailchimp's own words after a colon (: "API Key Invalid"), or nothing; dc: the data center, like us21

source.notifuseNoWorkspace: Notifuse rejected the API key: it isn't attached to a workspace.

source.unreachable.note: reason: the network's own words, like Timed out

source.rejectedKey.note: reason: the source's own words, or its HTTP status like 401 Unauthorized

source.answered.note: status: an HTTP status, like 503 Service Unavailable

source.refused.note: reason: the source's own words, or its HTTP status

source.redirects.message: {source} redirects to another address ({status}). Enter the address it answers at.
source.redirects.note: status: an HTTP status, like 301 Moved Permanently

source.unreadable.message: {source} sent a response ReputeCast can't read: {reason}.
source.unreadable.note: reason: the JSON decoder's own words

source.keyUnreadable.message: the stored API key can't be decrypted; paste it again
source.keyUnreadable.note: starts lowercase, as the error it replaces did; shown after the import's failure

file.unreadable.message: {file} can't be read: {reason, select, notXlsx {this isn't an .xlsx file (it can't be opened as a spreadsheet)} noWorkbook {this .xlsx file has no workbook} workbook {the workbook can't be read: {detail}} noSheets {the workbook has no sheets} missingSheet {the workbook points to {sheet}, which is missing} sharedStrings {the shared strings can't be read: {detail}} sheet {the sheet can't be read: {detail}} tooManyRows {the sheet has more than {max} rows} cell {a cell can't be read: {detail}} other {{detail}}}.
file.unreadable.note: file: the uploaded file's name; detail: the reader's own words; sheet: a part of the workbook, like xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml

file.rowUnreadable.message: {file}: row {row} can't be read ({reason, select, bareQuote {bare " in non-quoted-field} quote {extraneous or missing " in quoted-field} other {{detail}}}). Fix the file and upload it again.
file.rowUnreadable.note: a CSV row the reader stopped at; detail: the reader's own words

file.tooManyRows: {file} has more than {max} rows. Split it into smaller files.

file.badColumns.message: {file}: row {row} has {columns} columns, the header has {header}
file.badColumns.note: a CSV row with the wrong number of values; no full stop, as on the board

log.start.note: the live log's first line, followed by the lists (log.mapping) and the consent rule (log.consent), joined with ·

log.mapping.message: {kind, select, file {{source}} audience {audience {source}} group {group {source}} other {list {source}}} → list {target}
log.mapping.note: source: a file's name, or a source list's name in quotes; target: a ReputeCast list's name. audience is Mailchimp's word, group MailerLite's

log.consent: consent: {consent, select, repermission {re-permission everyone} source {keep source opt-in} other {trust double opt-in}}

log.pulled.note: providers: sending providers' names, as a list

log.batch: Batch {batch} · {rows} rows: {imported} imported, {merged} merged, {suppressed} suppressed, {skipped} skipped
log.stopped: Import stopped; contacts already imported stay
log.nextSync: {count} new suppressions reach {providers} with the next provider sync

log.repermissionFailed.note: reason: the failure in the sender's own words

log.repermissionSent: Sent {count} re-permission emails through the System stream
log.repermissionWaiting: {count} contacts wait for re-permission; connect a System provider to email them

log.analyzeFailed.note: the database's query planner; reason: the database's own words

log.failed.note: reason: the failure in the system's own words

log.retry.note: status: an HTTP status code, like 503

log.retry429.message: {source} returned 429 Too Many Requests; waiting {wait} before retrying
log.retry429.note: 429 Too Many Requests is the HTTP status, never translated; wait: like 2s or 1m0s

log.paused.message: {source} is rate-limiting us (429); paused, resuming at {at}

log.slowed: Slowed down to {pace} requests a second to {source}
log.templatesKey: Templates weren't imported: the stored API key can't be decrypted.

log.templatesFailed.note: reason: the failure in the system's own words

log.templates: Imported {transactional} transactional templates as drafts and {saved} saved templates
log.templatesManual: Imported {transactional} transactional templates as drafts and {saved} saved templates; {manual} need a manual fix

job.pausedResumes.note: time: a time of day, like 14:05

job.stoppedDetail: {processed} of {total} rows were processed before it stopped
job.etaMinutes: {n, plural, one {about 1 minute left} other {about # minutes left}}

consent.confirmed.message: Subscribed · confirmed, keep opt-in date and IP as evidence
consent.confirmed.note: what a source status becomes, in the Consent step's select

consent.pending: Subscribed · pending, send a re-permission email

consent.noteDoubleOptIn.message: double opt-in was on in this audience
consent.noteDoubleOptIn.note: under the source's status subscribed; audience is Mailchimp's word

consent.noteDoubleOptInSince.message: double opt-in was on in this audience since {year}

consent.noteHardBounced.note: under the source's status cleaned (Mailchimp's word)

consent.labelAbuse.note: Mailchimp's own status: archived and abuse are its words

consent.effectUnsub: Broadcasts and Automations blocked; System mail allowed. Can't be changed by an import.

consent.effectBlockedPushed.note: providers: sending providers' names, as a list

consent.effectConfirmed: Gets Broadcasts and Automations right away
consent.effectPending: No marketing mail until they confirm

consent.history.message: Imported from {source}{by, select, yes { by {name}} other {}}, {day}, status {status}
consent.history.note: how the consent history entry will read; name: the person importing; status: the source's own word, like subscribed

consent.historyEvidence.message: Imported from {source}{by, select, yes { by {name}} other {}}, {day}, status {status}, evidence OPTIN_TIME {evidence}
consent.historyEvidence.note: evidence: a date like 2025-03-02; OPTIN_TIME is Mailchimp's field name

consent.historyNoRow: Imported from {source}{by, select, yes { by {name}} other {}}, {day}

history.detailList.note: a consent history entry's detail; list: the source list's name in quotes; status: the source's own word, like subscribed

history.notePending: consent carried over as "pending" until re-permission

history.noteEvidence.note: date: like 2025-03-02; OPTIN_TIME is Mailchimp's field name

suppression.unsubscribed.note: a suppression's original code: the source's status

suppression.cleaned.note: cleaned is Mailchimp's word for addresses that hard bounced

suppression.abuse.note: abuse is Mailchimp's word for a spam complaint

suppression.context.note: where a suppression came from: an import from another email tool

field.emailRequired.note: a target of Map fields; email is the field's key

field.createNew.note: key: the new field's key, in quotes

risky.role.label.note: a group of risky addresses in the import preview

risky.role.why: info@, sales@, support@ are shared inboxes; high complaint rates
risky.disposable.label: Disposable domains
risky.disposable.why: temporary inboxes that expire and bounce
risky.typo.label: Likely typos
risky.typo.why: domain within one character of a major provider
risky.stale.label: Never engaged, 2+ years old

risky.stale.why.message: no open or click since {year} in {source}; most likely to be stale or recycled into spam traps

risky.trap.label: Known spam-trap patterns
risky.trap.why: domains and local parts HostRepute associates with trap networks
risky.catch_all.label: Catch-all domains
risky.catch_all.why: the domain accepts every address, so the mailbox can't be confirmed
risky.abuse.label: Known complainers
risky.abuse.why: the service lists these addresses for abuse reports
risky.unknown.label: Unknown
risky.unknown.why: the mail server didn't answer the service
action.fixTypo: Fix the domain and import, flagged for review

example.rating.note: member rating is Mailchimp's own term

merge.fills.note: fields: the contact fields the import fills, as a list

merge.tags: {n, plural, one {Merge · adds # tag, keeps consent} other {Merge · adds # tags, keeps consent}}

duplicate.onList.message: On suppression list · {reason, select, unsubscribe {unsubscribed} hard_bounce {hard bounced} complaint {complained} other {suppressed}} {day}

duplicate.empty.note: field: a field's name (field.first_name…) or a custom field's key

duplicate.joined.note: source: where the contact came from, like Mailchimp or Signup form · docs

duplicate.tier.note: tier: Active, Cooling, At risk or Sunset, as the audience screens name them

duplicate.file.note: where a contact came from when the import's file kind is unknown

fill.first_name.note: a contact field, in merge.fills and duplicate.empty

invalid.noMX.note: why an address is invalid: its domain can't receive mail

notify.title.note: the notification when an import finishes

notify.body: {suppressed} suppressed, {skipped} skipped. The report lists every skipped row.
